references.text: The bow shall be in the clouds, and I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth. God said to Noah: "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth."
God said: "Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate the day from the night. They shall serve as signs for seasons, days, and years."
It shall stand firm like the moon forever, a faithful witness in the skies.

This shall be for me like the waters of Noah. As I swore that the waters of Noah should no more flood the earth, so I swear that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you. For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be removed," says the Lord, who has compassion on you.
Like the rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the radiance around him. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord.
He who sat there had an appearance like jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow that looked like an emerald.
And I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head.
Expands the covenant from Genesis 9 to include all creation and concretizes peace by breaking the weapons of war.
Clear theological contrast: the bow as an instrument of judgment (Lamentations) versus the bow as a sign of ended judgment and grace (Genesis).
Connects the sign of the stability of natural law (the rainbow) with the concrete blessing of rain and the earth's fertility.
